request: Test with all PMR files on this computer plus the EDIT drive; assess whether Bella is cleaner/more elegant than previous PMR implementations.
scope: Read-only traversal and parsing of every case-insensitive .pmr regular-file path found in accessible locations. Includes genuine databases, copied fixtures and historical authored probes; not all are genuine Avid specimens.
buildRefresh: The PMR source was newer than the existing parser objects. Rebuilt both normal and ASan/UBSan libraries/test targets, relinked temporary probes and repeated all checks against the current source before recording this result. Earlier implementation receipt hashes remain historical.

build.sandbox: Both temporary probes aborted at Qt CPU-feature detection (neon) before test execution inside the sandbox; final probes ran outside it with user approval and passed. Rebuilt focused CTest suites passed inside the sandbox.

inventory.pattern: case-insensitive .pmr suffix, regular files including file symlinks
inventory.directoryPolicy: No symlink-directory following. Same device/inode directories walked once (includes APFS firmlink aliases).

inventoryRetry: Initial sandbox traversal and user-approved outside-sandbox retry found the same27 paths; final retry retained519 traversal errors (253EPERM,265EACCES,1EBADF). No permission settings were changed. Protected folders remain unsearched; no exhaustive-machine claim.
method: A temporary C++ executable links the actual Bella archive and QtCore, calls parsePmr once per original path, and fingerprints every returned full FileMobId, Filename, Project and optional MasterMobId in stored order. An independent bounded Python observer decodes the source bytes and compares outcomes/checks/eligibility/reference coverage/selectedset/version/count/fingerprint. Validation-only SHA256 reads and filesystem observations before/after are separate from Bella acquisition; original content was not written.
fingerprintConvention: Same Bella PMR full records v1 newline prefix; unsigned32 BE selected version/count; stored-order normalized FileMobId bytes, UTF8 Filename, UTF8 Project, normalized optional MasterMobId bytes; each field prefixed by unsigned32 BE byte length; absent master length0. SHA256 digest.

interpretation.malformedAreAuthoredTruncations: All3 failures are old September scanner-probe files, confirmed in their generator. They do not demonstrate corruption in live Avid databases.
interpretation.stabilityLimit: Equal observations before/after are evidence of stability during these checks, not an atomic snapshot guarantee.

comparativeReview.scope: Read-only review of24 PMR-changing commits and representative initialMay, August, September/preCanon86c500c and activeOldScanner implementations. Qualitative assessment, not a universal or performance ranking.
comparativeReview.judgment: Bella has a simpler compact retained model than activeOldScanner for its agreed purpose. Compared with86c500c, it is more explicit and handles the additional agreed reporting/verification/cancellation requirements, but is not uniformly simpler or shorter.
currentBellaTradeoffs: Selected usable v16 avoids decoding/retaining base values; base-only/fallback paths traverse base framing then decode it.
Selection/fallback and related report state need careful bookkeeping.
Coarse whole-file/set cancellation follows the chosen policy and is less granular than activeOldScanner.
Detailed old raw provenance is omitted under the agreed compact-data requirements.
comparativeReview.limits: Line counts include comments and different scope; do not imply elegance or speed. No best-ever claim, scan-time gain or memory reduction is established.

limits: No access to protected locations that rejected both traversals; no claim that every PMR in the filesystem exists in this inventory. Symlink directories were not followed, files inside archives were not unpacked, and alias directories were traversed once. Tests execute on arm64 only. Observed PMR bases2/8 and selected8/16, all little-endian. No forced live-change/cancel/I/O races or broad scan-time/peak-memory benchmark.
